cards.front: What did Java 9 add to the Stream API?
cards.back: takeWhile, dropWhile, ofNullable, and a three-argument iterate with a predicate
cards.extra: takeWhile stops at the first non-matching element — unlike filter, which keeps scanning the whole stream.

cards.back: Runs two collectors over the same stream and merges their results with a function — Java 12
cards.extra: One pass, two aggregates: averages plus counts, min plus max, without materialising the stream twice.

cards.front: How do threads communicate with each other in classic Java?
cards.back: wait(), notify() and notifyAll() on a shared monitor, always inside a synchronized block
cards.extra: wait releases the lock and parks the thread; notifyAll wakes all waiters to re-check their condition in a loop.

cards.front: What are the six states of a Java thread?
cards.extra: BLOCKED means waiting for a monitor; WAITING means waiting for another thread's signal. Read them with getState().

cards.front: What range do thread priorities have, and do they work?
cards.back: 1 to 10 (MIN_PRIORITY to MAX_PRIORITY) — and they are not portable
cards.extra: The OS decides; on many systems priorities are ignored. Correctness must never depend on them.

cards.front: What is the practical way to use thread pools?
cards.back: ExecutorService from Executors: submit tasks and reuse a bounded set of threads
cards.extra: Creating a thread per task is expensive and unbounded. A pool caps concurrency and reuses workers.

cards.back: They leave objects in an inconsistent state — the suspended thread may hold locks, and stop releases them mid-update
cards.extra: Interruption plus a flag is the safe replacement; the JVM cannot know where a safe suspension point is.

cards.front: What is a JVM shutdown hook?
cards.back: Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(Thread) — code that runs when the JVM is terminating normally or on SIGTERM
cards.extra: It does not run on kill -9 or a crash. Hooks run concurrently, so ordering between them is not guaranteed.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::13 JVM and Tooling::03 Core JDK Tools

cards.front: What is static binding versus dynamic binding?
cards.back: Static: resolved at compile time (private, static, final methods). Dynamic: chosen at run time from the object's actual type
cards.extra: Overloaded methods are bound statically by parameter types; overridden methods are bound dynamically. That split is the source of the classic overload surprise.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::14 Static vs Dynamic Binding

cards.front: What is a char in Java's Unicode model?
cards.back: A 16-bit UTF-16 code unit — not necessarily a whole character
cards.extra: Characters outside the BMP need two chars (a surrogate pair); use codePointAt, codePointCount and Character.isSupplementaryCodePoint to handle them.

cards.back: A compact growable array of bits, with and/or/xor and cardinality operations
cards.extra: It is far smaller than a boolean array and is used for flags, filters and set arithmetic over integers.

cards.back: They predate the collections framework, are fully synchronized, and expose old-style APIs
cards.extra: Use HashMap, ArrayList and the concurrent collections instead; Iteration over Vector/Hashtable is not fail-fast in the modern sense.

cards.back: A fixed-size view of the array — element assignment works, add and remove throw
cards.extra: It is a bridge from array to List, not a copy. List.of is immutable; the two behave differently on set().

cards.front: What is the Z Garbage Collector?
cards.back: A low-latency collector added in Java 11: concurrent, with pause times under a millisecond, at the cost of throughput
cards.extra: Pauses stay short regardless of heap size, which is why it suits large heaps with latency SLOs rather than batch throughput.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::13 JVM and Tooling::02 Garbage Collection

cards.front: What does ArrayList do when it runs out of capacity?
cards.back: Grows to about 1.5× the current capacity, copying the elements into a new array
cards.extra: That amortises to O(1) per append, but the copy is a real cost — pre-size the list when you know the count.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::04 Collections::01 Array vs ArrayList
